findings.source_passage: any man unaccustomed to such sights, to have looked over her side that night, would have almost thought the whole round sea was one huge cheese, and those sharks the maggots in it.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the single most quotable, rhetorically distinctive image in the chapter — the 'whole round sea was one huge cheese, and those sharks the maggots in it' is a signature Melvillean grotesque simile that critics return to repeatedly. Its total absence is a major signature loss.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore verbatim or near-verbatim: 'any man unaccustomed to such sights would have almost thought the whole round sea was one huge cheese, and those sharks the maggots in it.'

findings.source_passage: those entrails seemed swallowed over and over again by the same mouth, to be oppositely voided by the gaping wound.
findings.why_it_matters: The source's precise, grotesque phrasing 'to be oppositely voided by the gaping wound' is signature Melville — the clinical precision married to horror. The draft reduces it to 'to void them by the gaping wound,' losing the 'oppositely' and the passive construction that carry the rhetorical force.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'to be oppositely voided by the gaping wound' verbatim; the word 'oppositely' is load-bearing.

findings.source_passage: A sort of generic or Pantheistic vitality seemed to lurk in their very joints and bones, after what might be called the individual life had departed.
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'generic or Pantheistic vitality' is philosophically loaded and critically significant — it connects to Melville's larger meditation on animism, pantheism, and the nature of life. The draft reduces it to 'a pantheistic vitality lurked in joints and bones,' erasing 'generic or,' the epistemically hedged phrasing 'seemed to lurk,' and the qualifying clause 'after what might be called the individual life had departed,' all of which carry interpretive weight.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'A sort of generic or Pantheistic vitality seemed to lurk in their very joints and bones, after what might be called the individual life had departed.'

findings.source_passage: agonizingly lifting his hand up and down
findings.why_it_matters: The draft replaces 'agonizingly lifting his hand up and down' with 'lifting his hurt hand,' losing both the adverb 'agonizingly' and the kinetic repetition 'up and down' that physically enact Queequeg's pain and give his following theological punchline its tragicomic grounding.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'agonizingly lifting his hand up and down' verbatim in the speech tag.

summary: The draft's most damaging failure is the complete erasure of 'the whole round sea was one huge cheese, and those sharks the maggots in it' — the chapter's most famous and critically noted image — plus three additional medium-severity flattenings of signature philosophical and voice-defining passages.
